editorialSummary: Nothing captures modern progress quite like [climate talks collapsing](https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/arteseideas/cop31-avances-tecnicos-politicos-abren-camino-rumbo-bonn-africa-20261126-846013.html) while broken routers trigger a [nationwide flight outage](https://oglobo.globo.com/mundo/epoca/noticia/2026/11/25/investigadores-reproduzem-falha-que-suspendeu-voos-nos-eua-e-apontam-possivel-problema-em-roteador-veja-o-que-se-sabe.ghtml) and British discount giant [Poundland enters administration](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm3vgdn037z4o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss). Fortunately, astronomers examining a [stadium-sized asteroid crater](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw8dv112r5gmo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss) have confirmed we are at least getting better at smashing rocks into space.
